The -s flag then sees -b as its value, and the real subcommand token stays in the args passed on, instead of the intended [-s first -b].

matched.failure: A user's root command has a `BashCompletionFunction` that defines only `__custom_func` (the pattern the old docs show) and no `__<root>_custom_func`. Pressing tab on a noun position reaches the else branch, `declare -F ___custom_func` fails, and `__custom_func` is never called. COMPREPLY stays empty and completion silently stops working for that user, which is the regression the fallback was meant to prevent.
